title: Lago di Braies Seeweg circuit — enrichment dossier
researchMethod: ORMA desk research using current municipal/destination, provincial nature-park, human-approved parking and approved GPX evidence. No field visit or canopy raster analysis is claimed.
editorialSummary: ORMA Verified was restored by explicit human instruction accompanying export (20). The livestock claim remains supported by the editor's direct local knowledge of the exact Seeweg circuit. No livestock is expected around the lake; protected-area lead and wildlife-disturbance rules remain mandatory. Verification does not authorize publication.

requiredAcknowledgements.label: Retain the protected-area lead rule even though livestock is not expected.
Reopen the livestock claim if future local evidence or signage conflicts with the attestation.

claims.label: Seeweg circuit identity
claims.proposedValue: A complete walking circuit around Lago di Braies, starting and ending at the lake tavern/hotel area.
claims.evidenceSummary: The current itinerary names Seeweg, the same start/finish and a continuous circuit.
humanChecks: Keep this separate from partial western-shore walks.

claims.label: Approved route geometry
claims.evidenceSummary: The GPX closes exactly and measures 3.49 km, within 3.1% of the published 3.6 km.
humanChecks: Do not restore the earlier simplified stored line for metrics.

claims.label: Headline effort metrics
claims.proposedValue: 3.6 km, 39 m ascent/descent, approximately 1 hour, 1,492–1,531 m elevation.
claims.evidenceSummary: All figures are published together on the current route page.
humanChecks: Use official ascent because the reference GPX contains no elevation samples.

claims.label: Official parking choices
claims.proposedValue: Retain the human-approved official P1, P2, P3 and P4 set.
claims.evidenceSummary: The municipal system and human gate preserve the four choices; export (12) contained no revocation.
humanChecks: Recheck booking products and prices seasonally.

claims.label: 2026 valley access controls
claims.proposedValue: From 1 July–15 September 2026, 09:00–16:00, enter by public transport, walking, cycling or with a parking reservation/transit permit; shuttle booking is required.
claims.evidenceSummary: Current route and municipal pages publish the same controlled-access period and reservation requirement.
humanChecks: Link to live booking and do not hard-code availability or price.

claims.label: Dogs and transport
claims.proposedValue: The route is dog-friendly; keep dogs on lead in the nature park and carry/use a muzzle on public transport.
claims.evidenceSummary: The route is labelled dog-friendly, the provincial park code requires dogs on a lead, and the municipal page requires a muzzle on public transport.
humanChecks: Distinguish trail conduct from bus requirements in the UI.

claims.label: Mixed lakeshore surface and narrow sections
claims.proposedValue: The circuit includes broad forest/lakeshore paths plus narrower rooted sections, uphill steps and a section beside a vertical rock wall.
claims.evidenceSummary: Both current route descriptions distinguish the broad side from the narrower, rooted and stepped side.
humanChecks: Photograph and field-check the narrow/stepped section before assigning a dog difficulty score.
Do not describe the entire loop as stroller-compatible.

claims.label: Shade and heat exposure
claims.proposedValue: The circuit mixes tree/forest sections with open lakeshore and southern beaches; do not rely on continuous shade and do not publish a percentage.
claims.evidenceSummary: The current turn-by-turn route description explicitly moves between trees, a forest/lakeshore path and open southern beaches. This supports a qualitative mixed-shade statement only.
humanChecks: Account for reflected sun and crowds on open lakeshore sections.
Treat seasonal foliage and time-of-day shade as variable.

claims.label: Reliable dog water
claims.proposedValue: Carry all water your dog will need. No potable route source is verified, and Lago di Braies must not be presented as a drinking source.
claims.evidenceSummary: No reviewed official route or municipal source identifies a potable fountain. The sources identify the protected lake, hospitality and toilets, none of which establishes freely available dog water. ORMA therefore publishes a conservative carry-all-water instruction rather than claiming that no service exists.
humanChecks: Keep beaches and lake views as POIs, not water-source claims.
If a fountain is later verified, record exact coordinates, potability and seasonality before changing this instruction.

claims.label: Route POIs and facilities
claims.proposedValue: Boat house, picnic/rest areas, benches, southern beaches, toilets and the lake tavern/hotel area are route-linked facilities and POIs.
claims.evidenceSummary: The route narrative and municipal FAQ identify these locations/facilities.
humanChecks: Verify exact toilet season and accessibility before publication.

claims.label: Livestock and wildlife interaction
claims.proposedValue: No livestock is expected around the exact Seeweg lakeshore circuit. Keep dogs on lead because protected-area wildlife rules still apply.
claims.evidenceSummary: The human editor confirms from direct local knowledge that there is no livestock around the approved lakeshore circuit. This resolves the route-specific livestock objection without weakening the separate protected-area wildlife and lead requirements.
humanChecks: Do not infer that wildlife is absent.
Reopen this claim if new signage, reports or field evidence conflicts with the attestation.
Review annually before the principal hiking season.

claims.label: Publishable hero asset
claims.proposedValue: Use kallerna's recent geolocated southern-shore photograph as the initial hero under CC BY-SA 4.0, with full credit, licence link and change notice; retain operational field shots for later enrichment.
claims.evidenceSummary: The file page records creator kallerna, capture date 2 October 2025, coordinates 46.699886/12.087428 and CC BY-SA 4.0. The minimum launch-asset rule requires one fully provenanced hero; missing operational shots remain a Visual Director checklist, not evidence gaps.
humanChecks: Approve the exact credit and share-alike compliance plan before downloading or publishing.
Do not use the scenic image as evidence of trail accessibility or water suitability.
Keep roots/steps, rock wall, parking, toilet and dog-context shots on the enrichment checklist.
